headline_marked: [[Four national leaders killed in Dhaka Central Jail]] on November 3, 1975, with presidential consent
headline: Four national leaders killed in Dhaka Central Jail on November 3, 1975, with presidential consent
summary: The killings of Syed Nazrul Islam, Tajuddin Ahmed, M Mansur Ali, and AHM Qamaruzzaman occurred amid a fierce power struggle following Bangabandhu's assassination, with then-President Khandaker Mushtaque Ahmed's direct approval.
details: On November 3, 1975, four national leaders who had guided Bangladesh through its Liberation War were brutally murdered inside Dhaka Central Jail. The victims were Syed Nazrul Islam, Tajuddin Ahmed, M Mansur Ali, and AHM Qamaruzzaman.

This national tragedy unfolded amid a fierce power struggle within the military, following the assassination of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman on August 15, 1975. The four leaders had been imprisoned on politically motivated charges under martial law.

According to the Appellate Division's full verdict delivered on April 30, 2013, a chain of events began around 3:00 am on November 3. The then Inspector General of Prisons, Nuruzzaman Howlader, received several calls from army personnel at Bangabhaban, instructing him to go to Dhaka Central Jail.

Upon arrival, Nuruzzaman continued to receive calls, and sometime later, Captain Moslem Uddin arrived at the jail gate with four armed personnel. They inquired if the four leaders had been kept separately as instructed and plainly announced their intention to put the men to death.

Nuruzzaman then sought to speak to President Khandaker Mushtaque Ahmed. The verdict states that Mushtaque instructed Nuruzzaman over the phone to let the five army personnel "do whatever they wanted to do."
Following this, the armed men entered the prison and opened fire on the four leaders. After Fajr prayers, Nuruzzaman learned that another group of armed personnel had arrived to confirm the kills.
They discovered that two of the four leaders were still alive and proceeded to kill them with bayonets. This ensured the completion of the brutal act.

Years later, retired Brigadier General M Sakhawat Hussain wrote that the murder of the four leaders took place "with the informed consent of Rashid and Mushtaque." He also noted that Major General Khalilur Rahman was aware of the killings.

Sakhawat's book "Roktakto Dingulo: 1975-81" recalled that the massacre occurred in the dead of night, coinciding with a counter-coup, and was carried out in a planned manner under Moslem's leadership.

Moslem himself claimed to have personally killed the imprisoned leaders with a burst of fire from a Sten gun. Thus, one of the most brutal murders in Bangladesh's history was carried out with the consent of the highest level of the state.

headline_marked: ICT prosecution [[charges 7 Awami League leaders]] over July uprising crimes
headline: ICT prosecution charges 7 Awami League leaders over July uprising crimes
summary: The formal charge, submitted to the International Crimes Tribunal, alleges their involvement in planning and implementing a state policy to suppress the 2024 July uprising.
details: The prosecution yesterday submitted a formal charge to the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against seven Awami League leaders. They are accused of alleged crimes against humanity during the July uprising in 2024.

The accused include former ministers Amir Hossain Amu, Abdur Razzaque, Shahjahan Khan, Dipu Moni, Mirza Azam, Faruk Khan, and former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s energy adviser Taufiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury. Six are currently in jail, while Mirza Azam remains absconding.

Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim stated that the accused allegedly helped plan, facilitate, and implement a state policy to suppress the uprising. He added that the then government adopted the suppression as state policy.

The Awami League and the 14-party alliance also reportedly took political decisions to crush the movement. The accused, as influential members and policymakers, allegedly participated in and contributed to the crackdown.

Evidence submitted by the prosecution includes recordings of conversations involving Sheikh Hasina and the accused. The United Nations fact-finding report on the July uprising was also presented as evidence.
